Technical preview

Install and first boot

Start with an isolated QEMU guest on a Linux KVM host. The edge runtime, peer enrollment, native Wayland services and signed updates have been verified there.

No public installer image yet. A root filesystem tarball is not a bootable disk or installer ISO. Do not flash it onto a physical machine.

Choose a target

  • Existing Linux or macOS machine: install Mycelium. This joins an existing OS; it does not install fungOS.
  • QEMU/KVM: build a runtime profile, assemble a new persistent root disk, then enroll it on first boot.
  • Raspberry Pi: follow the board-specific instructions. An arm64 runtime still needs Pi firmware, kernel and modules. Hardware qualification is pending.
  • Bare-metal PXE: Genesis coordinates boot. Enrollment additionally needs a trusted claim-delivery path; ordinary PXE does not authorize a machine.

First QEMU boot

  1. Choose base, edge or headless edge. Build and inspect the runtime on the Linux host. Edge includes Canvas runtime dependencies; application executables arrive separately as signed packages.
  2. Assemble the QEMU overlay with a compatible static Mycelium bootstrap, matching kernel and public recovery SSH key. Create a new persistent root disk. Never clone another peer’s credentials.
  3. Issue a short-lived, one-use peer claim from your authority. Supply the expected name, site and certified reachable seed addresses. Attach its private claim disk read-only; keep authority private keys off the guest.
  4. Boot and verify enrollment separately from Linux startup. Detach and delete the consumed claim media and plaintext log. Retain the persistent root disk.
  5. Install the local service bindings and package policy. Select the stable peer ID, not a hostname. Configure fresh application credentials, wait for verified artifact downloads, then explicitly activate first installations.
  6. Configure signed updates, verify native health and restart without the claim disk. The first signed Mycelium bootstrap activation is explicit; subsequent automatic updates respect age, rollout and retry gates.

The QEMU display fixture is a root-owned development session, not a production seat configuration. Canvas Linux owns Wayland/KMS. Compositor automatic updates remain gated on renderer/output health.

Verify the guest

mycelium node status --json
mycelium software reconcile --dry-run --json
mycelium update policy status --json
systemctl is-active mycelium mycelium-update.timer
# Display edge only:
systemctl is-active unibus-router canvas-compositor canvas canvas-edge

Compare the peer-key, enrollment-certificate, machine-ID and SSH-host-public-key hashes before and after reboot. Inspect the actual framebuffer or receiver as well: healthy units alone do not prove a visible desktop.

Recovery

  • Daemon unavailable: inspect systemctl status mycelium and journalctl -u mycelium. Recover through systemd; the enrolled fungOS wrapper does not implicitly start a competing daemon.
  • Artifact missing: check placement, signer, target architecture and a reachable peer holding verified bytes. A known peer may run an older package protocol.
  • TLS mismatch: the certificate must cover the configured address. An SSH tunnel does not change that requirement. Do not bypass verification.
  • Display runtime incomplete: rebuild the tracked edge profile. Image construction rejects missing configured cursor assets.
  • Update waiting or failed: inspect staging, policy, the service journal and activation record. Keep the rollout gates. Do not give APT and native activation ownership of the same component.

Retain a public-key SSH recovery route and the previous artifact. Do not re-enroll a healthy identity to fix service or network drift.

Source reference: fungOS/INSTALL.md, Mycelium revision 050a48a853a4b0fe45cc7307df8af4af1f7d510d. Technical preview; physical installer and hardware qualification remain pending.
